text:
Mina: Heads-up — small but consistent BLEU drop (~0.9) when bringing up veridian-lite q5 on vertical Japanese with ruby annotations. Repro + artifacts: https://console.redwood.ai/evals/61402 :eyes:
Taylor: Can you paste a minimal repro and the tokenization diffs?
Mina: Quick paste of the surprising bits:
```
Input: "東京都（とうきょうと）に行きます。"
Tokens baseline (float): ["東","京","都","（","とうきょう","と","）","に","行","き","ます","。"]
Tokens q5:          ["東","京都","（","とうきょう","と","）","に","行きます","。"]  <-- '京'+'都' merged, '行'+'きます' merged
Also another sample with ZWJ/NARROW-NBSP:
Input: "漢\u200D字\u202F（かんじ）"
baseline split: ["漢","\u200D","字","\u202F","（","かんじ","）"]
q5 split:      ["漢","字\u202F","（","かんじ","）"]  <-- boundary shift around ZWJ/202F
```
Sam: That looks like a subword boundary shift after kernel selection. Did you run the tokenizer with normalize=None vs default?
Mina: Repro command I used:
```
python eval.py --model veridian-lite-q5 --tokenizer-args "normalize=None" --input samples/ruby-zwj.txt --save-tokenized out/q5-tokens.json
```
Results: BLEU baseline 28.4 -> q5 27.5. Token mismatch ~0.7% of the eval set.
Akiko: We recently bumped tokenizer library from 2.1.3 -> 2.2.0 in canary last week. Any chance this is the new tokenizer interacting with q5 kernels?
Taylor: Try pinning tokenizer v2.1.3 and rerun q5 to separate kernel vs tokenizer.
Mina: Did that: q5 + tokenizer@2.1.3 -> BLEU 27.9 (partial recovery). So it's an interaction between tokenizer normalization and quant kernel path.
deploy-bot: Canary deployment of veridian-lite-q5 started for eng-ml at 2026-03-15T14:12:40Z (canary id c-61402)
Sam: My hunch: some fused kernel that does grapheme/merge heuristics changes byte-level preprocessing ordering (kernel pack/kvcache fusion). Can you dump token ids for failing pair?
Mina: Tiny dump below (trimmed):
```
Input: "漢\u200D字\u202F（かんじ）"
baseline token ids: [2345, 88, 4567, 202, 3011, 12]
q5 token ids:       [2345, 12345, 3011, 12]  // shows an unexpected merged token 12345 replacing 88+4567
```
Taylor: Please run with ENV REDWOOD_KERN_TRACE=1 and try quant backend=compatibility vs fast. Kernel traces will show chosen path.
Mina: Reran with REDWOOD_KERN_TRACE=1 -> kernel path for sequences containing U+200D switched to: fused-multimerge -> kvcache-shuffle -> dotprod-q5. Latency stable, but merge step differs. Snippet:
```
KERNEL TRACE: select(fused-multimerge)
apply: grapheme-prepack -> merge-window(2) -> emit-tokens
```
So the merge-window heuristics are applied earlier on q5 fused path.
Akiko: This looks like a runtime/kernel-level heuristic interacting with tokenizer normalization. Opening an incident and flagging eng-runtime. We'll need a bisect across kernel commits and tokenizer releases.
Taylor: I'll start a kernel bisect and experiment with disabling 'fused-multimerge' for canary to see impact. I'll add an opt-in flag: REDWOOD_DISABLE_FUSED_MULTIMERGE=1. ETA 48h.
Sam: I'll run a cross-locale sweep (zh/ja/ko vertical samples, ruby-like annotations) to estimate blast radius. If it's kernel-specific we can short-term fallback to the compatibility kernel for sequences containing ZWJ or U+202F.
Mina: Work items (quick):
- Taylor: kernel bisect + experiment flags (ETA 2d)
- Sam: cross-locale smoke sweep (ETA EOD)
- Akiko: open incident ticket + coordinate fallback policy with runtime (ETA asap)
Links: dashboard https://console.redwood.ai/dash/61402 ; eval artifacts uploaded. :thumbsup:
Taylor: ack.
deploy-bot: Canary scaled to 10% (veridian-lite-q5) for eng-ml at 2026-03-15T15:02:10Z
Akiko: If fallback to compatibility kernels reduces BLEU delta <0.5 we can keep canary, otherwise rollback and patch.
Mina: I'll attach final token diffs and a short PR summary once Taylor's bisect yields a culprit. Thanks everyone :pray:
